saw_lines: Cast iron is bought once for decades, so buyers judge the promise of lasting, not the pan itself.
So the sale is won by proof a buyer can believe on the first look, before they weigh the price.
Your site leads with 2,600 years of iron, yet 0 of 29 ads carry a proof number. Put 2,600 years on the creative and open two ads with a review quote.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: Your site leads with 2,600 years of iron, yet 0 of 29 ads carry a proof number, so premium buyers have nothing to trust before the click. Put 2,600 years on the creative and open two ads with a review quote.

Your guarantee arrives after 72% of the copy on a median ad of 122 words, so the reason to buy comes last. Move the Three Generation Guarantee into the first two lines of every ad, then state the price right after it.

Your median ad runs 122 words and the longest runs 235 words, so the hook gets buried under detail. Cut every ad to two lines plus the offer, and send the rest to the product page where the detail belongs.

Your 29 copy ads open with 20 different stories, so no opener builds recognition. The biggest, the josh emett opening, leads just 3 ads. Choose the two strongest openings and build the next batch from them with three variations each.

ads_1: Marriage and josh emett openers, with 2,600 years of iron as the proof line
